literal: Glory to a person is the wealth of determination; disgrace to a person is thinking 'we shall live' having lost that.
translation: A person's glory is the wealth of their inner determination; their disgrace is thinking, 'We shall live on,' after having lost that determination.
modern: ஒருவனுக்குப் பெருமை என்பது அவனது ஊக்கமாகிய செல்வமே ஆகும்; அவனுக்கு இழிவு என்பது அந்த ஊக்கத்தை இழந்துவிட்டும் 'நாம் உயிர் வாழ்வோம்' என்று நினைப்பதே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines true greatness and disgrace through the lens of inner strength. Glory is described as the wealth of determination that a person possesses. In contrast, disgrace is the attitude of wanting to live on after losing that noble determination. The poet suggests that a life devoid of high aspirations and self-respect is a shameful existence, whereas a life driven by strong willpower is truly glorious.
